objective: Verify worker thread modules trigger same-process CLI restart when they change under --hmr, including eval workers that load an application module
method: Built target/debug/quench-node, then ran two temporary CommonJS applications. The first spawned a file-backed worker, atomically replaced worker.cjs from generation 1 to 2, and observed the parent and worker restart. The second spawned an eval worker that required an absolute application dep.cjs path, edited the dependency from generation 1 to 2, and observed restart. Also compared process method API shapes against the local Node oracle.

node_oracle.comparison: hrtime and hrtime.bigint types; cpuUsage and threadCpuUsage keys; memoryUsage keys and positive rss; resourceUsage keys and numeric maxRSS

implementation: Worker source paths are registered with the parent HMR graph and use restart fallback. Eval workers have a virtual graph so loaded files are tracked even if the importer has no filesystem path. Darwin process_methods now uses task_info for current RSS, Mach thread_info for thread CPU, and converts ru_maxrss bytes to KiB per pinned libuv source.
scope: Focused runtime smokes on one macOS host. Process metric values naturally differed between Node and Quench; this compared observable result shapes and units, not performance or exact machine-dependent counters.
result: Both file-backed and eval worker changes restarted the main CLI invocation in the original PID and loaded generation 2.
